paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is the One doing the inviting, and He doesn't ask you to bring a thing. He says, "Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you without money, come, buy, and eat!" (Isaiah 55:1). Nobody gets turned away at the door because their pockets are empty. All He asks is that you listen, "so that your soul may live" (Isaiah 55:3).

Now, the passage also says what happens when we chase things that don't satisfy. The LORD asks, "Why spend money on that which is not bread, and your labor on that which does not satisfy?" (Isaiah 55:2). So the call is to turn back while He can be found, because He "will freely pardon" (Isaiah 55:6-7). And if you ever wonder how that's possible, He says, "My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways" (Isaiah 55:8), and His mercy is bigger than what we'd come up with.

Then He gives you something to lean on: His word. It "will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it" (Isaiah 55:11). So when you open the Bible, you're not wasting your time, because God's word is doing its work. And that's why I can say it with a big smile, friend: come hungry, come empty-handed, and come back tomorrow, because the table's still set.
